agent.summary: The scene is a small, enclosed back patio at dusk. It has dark brick-pattern paving, a brick house wall with a large sliding glass door into a lit living room, and planted beds, trees and slatted fences on the other sides. I set the house wall (#0) to solid. I split the sliding-door glass off it as a new candidate (#40), widened it to cover both panes, and set it to window, because the furnished, lit room behind is clearly visible and should keep its own depth. I also trimmed #0 back from the climbing plants beside the door. I merged four stacked floor candidates (#1, #9, #15, #16) into one paving surface (#41). It and the other paving floors (#4, #6, #26) are solid. I cut the parts of #4, #6 and #41 that ran into the planted beds so that the floor rule can't remove the plants. I set the leftovers to ignore: the door-sill fragment (#33), the room floor seen through the glass (#36), the thin sliver at the door frame (#34), and all the sloped or low-concentration candidates, which are slices through trees, hedges and sky. I didn't add the fences or the far rendered wall, because they're mostly hidden behind dense planting and a wrong solid rule would remove that planting. One thing is left as is: on the top-down map, #0 still runs past the east edge of the patio. Looking along the wall (v00/f00162), it does seem to be the house front carrying on, so the extension is probably real. That part is hidden behind bushes in the photos I checked, so I couldn't select it to cut it off.
